gap: No result ChatGPT got says that BLUETTI's own US store sells the Elite 100 V2 + 200W Solar bundle for $729, $169 less than buying the Elite 100 V2 ($499) and the 200W panel ($399) separately. Its product page also lists no solar cable in the box, and the 20 A MC4-to-XT60 cable that connects the panel's MC4 plugs to the station is marked out of stock and discontinued.
standout_why: Neither cited page names a product, store, bundle, connector or cable. solar.com (guide-to-balcony-plug-in-solar) gives only generic kit price bands, such as $285–$800 for 180–400 W starters, and says nothing about power station input voltage or connectors. pluginsolartracker.com (California) covers only the law: 1,200 W per dwelling, certification and anti-islanding protection. ChatGPT's own answer shows an EcoFlow Delta 3 Classic + 160W kit at $669 and an Anker C300 + 60W kit at $399.99, but nothing about bundle savings, connectors or the panel-to-station cable. This is a 2 rather than a 3 because the box contents conflict: BLUETTI's store page lists no solar cable, while a search snippet says the official manual lists a 1.5 m MC4-to-XT60 cable. I could not open that manual.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W at 120 V, 12–60 V and 20 A solar input). It works without any utility connection, so a renter can use it now. Plug-in grid-tie kits are not yet legal in California and won't be until Jan 1, 2027.

Solar panel: BLUETTI SP200L 200 W foldable panel (MC4, Voc 24.6 V). It comes in the store's own $729 bundle. Two in series give 49.2 V, which is inside the 60 V input limit. Three in series give 73.8 V, which is over it.
Panel-to-station cable: BLUETTI Solar Charging Cable, 20 A MC4 to XT60 ($29). The store lists Elite 100 V2 as compatible, and the Elite 100 V2 store page lists no solar cable in the box.
Optional: BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable, MC4, 5 m ($59) or 10 m ($79). It lets the panel hang outside on the balcony while the station stays indoors.
